subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should ordinary Discord and bound ACP/sub-agent thread messages bypass busy channel/reply admission to reach active-run queue policy by default, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 or a successor be the canonical implementation path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but choosing where ordinary chat messages bypass serialization affects message ordering, session-state ownership, and fallback delivery across channels.

options.title: Refresh the admission-layer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 or a rebased successor as the canonical path, with explicit fallback/session-state tests and Discord ACP/sub-agent proof.

options.title: Keep explicit controls only
options.body: Support mid-turn steering through /steer, /acp steer, and equivalent control commands while documenting that ordinary bound-thread text remains queued for now.

options.title: Close this as scoped under canonical steering
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 as the only remaining tracker and close this issue only after preserving the Discord ACP/sub-agent evidence there.

recommendation.title: Refresh the admission-layer PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 or a rebased successor as the canonical path, with explicit fallback/session-state tests and Discord ACP/sub-agent proof.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent work and review context cover the active-run steering and reply/session-state surfaces where this product decision lands.
